item.title: Corporate Purpose and Socio-Technical Innovation: A Strategic Perspective
item.content:encoded:
Raffaella Montera, Sapienza University of Rome

Mario Tani, University of Naples Federico II

Carlos Rey Peña, UIC Barcelona University

Nicole Steller, ESCP Business School

This special issue examines how corporate purpose and socio-technical systems co-evolve, integrating these concepts within strategic management. As shareholder primacy faces challenges amid systemic fragility and institutional distrust, corporate purpose has become essential for clarifying organizational existence and societal value creation. Digital transformation driven by AI, platforms, and analytics further complicates this landscape, as technical architectures embed values and governance assumptions that shape economic behavior and sustainability outcomes.

The special issue addresses a central strategic tension: the efficiency-driven logic of algorithmic management often conflicts with the long-term, multi-stakeholder commitments required by authentic corporate purpose. The collection welcomes conceptual, empirical, and analytical submissions using diverse methodologies—qualitative, quantitative, mixed-methods, experimental, and case studies—that explore how purpose guides technology deployment and how digital tools operationalize and measure purpose-driven innovation across organizational, board, business model, and ecosystem levels.

Appel publié par Journal of strategy and management. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Dynamic capabilities and the strategic enactment of purpose through digital technologies
  • Resource orchestration for purpose-driven AI and data ecosystems
  • The strategic paradox of short-term algorithmic efficiency versus long-term purpose realization
  • Stakeholder strategy, legitimacy, and accountability in purpose-driven socio-technical systems
  • Digital ecosystems as strategic configurations of purposeful identity
  • Boards, leadership, and purpose-driven business models in the digital economy
